o1.biggest_strength: Three fixes ranked by money with the working shown, and each message written in voice with one button.
o1.biggest_mistake: The £61,000–£97,000 'sales kept' figure inflates the swap benefit by valuing every swap at the full £58 AOV when it should be margin on saved returns, and the exchange targets (35–45%) sit oddly against that.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Ground the swap value in gross profit on returns saved rather than full AOV, and tighten the copy so every line sounds like Jess and Amira.

o2.biggest_strength: It catches the signals the owner cares about — fit quiz moved up, a size-switch window in the order confirmation, a post-delivery fit-check for bras — and names the swap sales figure honestly as a ceiling.
o2.biggest_mistake: The headline '£11,830–£19,770 saved' adds ticket and return savings that partly overlap (a fit quiz returns fewer parcels and so also removes some tickets), overstating total savings.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Show one clean total with the overlap removed and margins, not raw sales, for swaps.

reason: Output 2 feels like it was written by someone who has read our returns reasons and our customers' words, with better messages for Jess and Amira. Output 1 is tighter and more usable, but its bigger swap-sales number is the kind of overstatement I would have to correct.
